materials.name: LiNbO3, favorable r33 orientation
materials.mechanismNotes: Strong, mature Pockels material; bulk common-mode response is not switchable kappa unless domain/orientation contrast is engineered.

materials.name: LiTaO3, favorable r33 orientation
materials.mechanismNotes: Similar EO scale to LiNbO3 with potentially lower photorefractive risk; still needs differential grating response.
materials.source: LiTaO3 r33 literature values near 30.5 pm/V at 632.8 nm.

materials.name: KTP-family crystal
materials.mechanismNotes: Mature Pockels-cell material; lower n keeps bulk index shift similar to LN despite comparable r.

materials.name: High-r33 EO polymer
materials.mechanismNotes: Large r33 can reduce voltage, but long-term stability, poling, optical loss, and large-aperture uniformity are major gates.
materials.source: EO-polymer reviews and manufacturer/literature reports above 100 pm/V.

materials.name: BaTiO3 / related ferroelectric
materials.mechanismNotes: Very large tensor components are reported in thin-film/waveguide contexts; centimeter-scale free-space bulk planes are not demonstrated.
materials.source: BTO photonics literature reports r42 near 1300 pm/V in favorable geometries.

domainEngineering.bulkLargeApertureStatus: Research-only at optical-period pitch; demonstrated submicron periods are thin-film or waveguide scale, not proven for centimeter free-space planes.

crossTalk.note: Best reduced-order confinement if guard layers or grounded neighbors are allowed.
Field fringing is comparable to plane pitch without full FEM optimization.
Can shape lateral field but introduces spatial nonuniformity and optical-metal routing risk.
Low optical insertion loss but poor individual depth selectivity at 1 mm pitch.

concepts.name: Periodically poled LiNbO3 switchable grating
concepts.decision: Most physically aligned with switchable kappa, but optical-period domain pitch and aperture scaling are major barriers.

concepts.name: EO-polymer differential-index grating
concepts.decision: Field scale is plausible only if a low-loss periodic differential material grating can be fabricated and stabilized.

concepts.name: Domain-engineered BaTiO3-like ferroelectric grating
concepts.decision: Large tensor response is attractive, but bulk/free-space/aperture maturity is the limiting gap.

concepts.name: Resonantly enhanced EO defect plane
concepts.decision: Material index shift becomes easier, but spectral, angular, thermal, and fabrication tolerance dominate.
